speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash and when it first appeared? Has the fever persisted, or has it resolved?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash appear to be a blanching, erythematous maculopapular eruption that looks like a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face? I also need to know if she has experienced any joint pain or swelling recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic trunk and extremity rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, the diagnosis is clear despite the negative serology which may be due to the timing of the test. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
